**Pathology** is an American death metal band from San Diego, California, formed in 2006 by drummer Dave Astor (Ex member and co founder of The Locust and Cattle Decapitation). Known for their brutal and aggressive sound, the band has released several albums and gained a dedicated following within the death metal community. Their lyrics often revolve around themes of gore, violence, and medical pathology. The band's lineup has changed over the years, but they continue to create intense and uncompromising music.
In 2006, the band released _Surgically Hacked_ (Amputated Vein Records) which was followed by a full-length debut _Incisions of Perverse Debauchery_ (Grindhead Records) and then _Age of Onset_ (Comatose Records, 2009), the album which led to a contract with Victory Records[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pathology_(band)#cite_note-victory_records-3) where the acclaimed _Legacy of the Ancients_ was released on July 6, 2010.

The band began extensive touring (with Nile, with Immolation, Vader, Obituary and Deicide, and with Deströyer 666, among others) but in November a horrible van accident derailed the band from continuing. At that point, the original vocalist Matti Way was replaced by Jonathan Huber (formerly of I Declare War). Guitarist Tim Tiszczenko, who at one point departed to be replaced by Kevin Schwartz, returned to form a guitar tandem with the latter.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pathology_(band)#cite_note-blabber_pathology-4) In May 2011, it was announced that Pathology would enter Lambesis Studios that summer with producer Daniel Castleman to begin working on a new full-length expected in Autumn. On August 30, the band was to start the US tour supporting Grave and Blood Red Throne.
On December 18, 2012, it was announced via the band's official site that they have fulfilled their three-album contract with Victory Records and that both original vocalist Matti Way and original guitarist Tim Tiszczenko have returned to the band.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pathology_(band)#cite_note-5) It was also announced that they will have a new album out later in 2013 on their new underground label Sevared Records. Vocalist Jonathan Huber left the band in December of that same year because Astor allegedly did not want the band to tour anymore and Huber stated that there was "no point in being in a non-touring band."
Pathology released their seventh full-length studio album _Lords of Rephaim_ on September 3, 2013.
After a successful $4,000 Kickstarter campaign, Pathology released their eighth full-length album _Throne of Reign_ on August 5, 2014.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pathology_(band)#cite_note-6)
On May 12, 2017, the band announced their self-titled ninth album would be released on July 21, and also released a new song from the album, "Lamentation".[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pathology_(band)#cite_note-7)

On February 6, 2018, the band announced the addition of vocalist Riley McShane (from Allegaeon) and guitarist Daniel Richardson.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pathology_(band)#cite_note-8) On May 22, it was announced that McShane had departed the band and was replaced by Clayton Meade. On July 30, it was revealed Obie Flett was the band's new vocalist, who was previously in the band in 2010.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pathology_(band)#cite_note-9)
On May 24, 2019, the band announced their tenth album, _Reborn to Kill_, would be released on August 9.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pathology_(band)#cite_note-10)
On August 27, 2021, the band announced they had signed to Nuclear Blast and that their eleventh album, _The Everlasting Plague_, would be released on November 19. They also released a new song from the album, "Engaging in Homicide".[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pathology_(band)#cite_note-11)
On March 26, 2024, the band announced their twelfth album, _Unholy Descent_, would be released on May 17, and also released a new song from the album, "Cult of the Black Triangle".[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pathology_(band)#cite_note-12) In August 2024, the band announced that guitarist Daniel Richardson would be leaving for personal reasons, with Kevin Schwartz returning to the lineup, who had previously played on _Awaken to the Suffering_ and _The Time of Great Purification_.
On August 4, 2026, the band announced the departure of Obie Flett, and revealed Tripp Taylor as the new vocalist of the band.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pathology_(band)#cite_note-13)

### Pathology Biography by Dave Donnelly
[![Image 1: Incisions of Perverse Debauchery](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/this.src='https://fastly-gce.allmusic.com/images/no_image/album_100x100.png')](https://www.allmusic.com/album/incisions-of-perverse-debauchery-mw0001983371 "Incisions of Perverse Debauchery") Pathology is a brutal American death metal band whose lineup has evolved considerably since their founding in 2006. The group's extreme sound combines gruesome shock imagery with hardcore influences, blastbeats, and distinctive gurgled vocals displayed prominently on the acclaimed 2009 offering Incisions of Perverse Debauchery. After signing to Victory Records that year, they issued the concept album Legacy of the Ancients in 2010. By the time the band had released Lords of Rephaim in 2013, they had woven a trace of traditional death metal into their sound, making their sonic presence even heavier. That direction was pushed to even greater extremes on 2017's self-titled offering, 2019's Reborn to Kill, and 2021's Nuclear Blast-issued Everlasting Plague. Three years later, Unholy Descent arrived on Agonia Records.
Pathology formed in 2006 in San Diego, California at the behest of Dave Astor, founding member and drummer of grindcore act the Locust and death metal group Cattle Decapitation. Astor was joined by vocalists Levi Fuselier and Matti Way, both formerly of legendary California death metal act Disgorge, and guitarist Tim Tiszczenko in the original four-piece lineup.

### Pathology Biography by Dave Donnelly
[![Image 2: Age of Onset](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/this.src='https://fastly-gce.allmusic.com/images/no_image/album_100x100.png')](https://www.allmusic.com/album/age-of-onset-mw0001736415 "Age of Onset") Pathology quickly built up a following in their native San Diego and released their first recording -- a demo CD entitled Surgically Hacked -- within a few months of their formation. The group's first full-length album, Incisions of Perverse Debauchery, was released in February of 2008 on Grindhead Records. Following the release of the album, Mason Gregory joined the band as a second guitarist and vocalist, replacing Fuselier. A second full album, Age of Onset, was released in June of the following year on Comatose Records.
Age of Onset brought Pathology to the attention of large Chicago hardcore/metal label Victory Record, though not before the group parted company with vocalist Matti Way, who was briefly replaced by Pascual Romero. Romero's tenure with the band was short, and he was soon asked to leave in order to accommodate Way's return and the addition of bassist Oscar Ramirez. The group's third album, Legacy of the Ancients, was released on Victory Records in July of 2010. The band was involved in a serious van accident while on tour with Nile in late 2010, forcing them to pull out of the remainder of the tour.

### Pathology Biography by Dave Donnelly
[![Image 3: Awaken to the Suffering](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/this.src='https://fastly-gce.allmusic.com/images/no_image/album_100x100.png')](https://www.allmusic.com/album/awaken-to-the-suffering-mw0002194146 "Awaken to the Suffering") In 2011, Way once again parted company with the band and was replaced by former I Declare War frontman Jonathan Huber. Tim Tiszczenko also left the band briefly, and was replaced by Kevin Schwartz and Stephen Parker, but soon returned in Parker's stead to form a dual guitar partnership with Schwartz. In September of 2011, the band released their fourth full-length record, Awaken to the Suffering, on Victory Records.
[![Image 4: The Time of Great Purification](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/this.src='https://fastly-gce.allmusic.com/images/no_image/album_100x100.png')](https://www.allmusic.com/album/the-time-of-great-purification-mw0002410811 "The Time of Great Purification")Huber left after 2012's The Time of Great Purification. Way returned for the tour and remained in the lineup for the next four years, singing on Lords of Rephaim (2013), Throne of Reign (2014), and Pathology (2017), by which time Tiszczenko also departed and was replaced by guitarist Dan Richardson. The lineup of Astor, Richardson, singer Obie Flett, and bassist Ricky Jackson issued Reborn to Kill in 2019. In 2021, Pathology inked a deal with Nuclear Blast and announced their 11th studio album, the COVID-19 pandemic-inspired concept effort Everlasting Plague, which was released later that November. The uncompromising Unholy Descent, released via Agonia Records, appeared three years later and saw guitarist Daniel Richardson depart for personal reasons, with longtime fan favorite Kevin Schwartz rejoining the band. In 2026, Tripp Taylor took over vocal duties from Obie Flett.

October 29, 2026
The Pathology band is heading into its 20th year with a new singer and a finished record. The San Diego brutal death metal outfit that drummer Dave Astor founded in early 2006 named Tripp Taylor its new vocalist on Aug. 4, said its 13th studio album is in the final stages of mixing and mastering, and has one show on the books: Sunday, Nov. 29, at the Whisky a Go Go in West Hollywood, opening for Fear Factory and Darkest Hour.
Astor is the only founding member still in **Pathology**. Around him, the band has cycled through singers, guitarists and bassists, released records on labels from Japan to Victory Records to Nuclear Blast, survived a van wreck in North Dakota, spent more than five years as a studio-only project and come back with some of the best reviews of its career. This is SDMETAL’s first feature on the band, so here is the whole story, from Astor’s years in The Locust and Cattle Decapitation to what we know, and don’t know, about album 13.

## Pathology Band at a Glance
*   **Formed:** Early 2006, San Diego  
*   **Founder:** Dave Astor (drums), the only original member left  
*   **Genre:** Brutal death metal  
*   **Studio albums:** 12, with a 13th finished and being mixed and mastered  
*   **Current lineup:** Dave Astor (drums), Kevin Schwartz (guitar), Ricky Jackson (bass), Tripp Taylor (vocals)  
*   **Next show:** Sunday, Nov. 29, Whisky a Go Go, West Hollywood

## Dave Astor, The Locust and Cattle Decapitation
Astor was born in San Diego on July 18, 1978, according to **Metal Archives**, and he was part of the city’s extreme music scene long before Pathology existed. Metal Archives lists him as the drummer in The Locust from 1994 to 2001. In Cattle Decapitation, it has him on vocals and bass in 1996 and on drums from 1996 to 2003. He played drums on _Human Jerky_ (1999) and is credited with drums and songwriting on _Homovore_ (2000) and _To Serve Man_ (2002). Pathology’s own bio goes further and calls him a “co-founder of THE LOCUST and CATTLE DECAPITATION.” Our **Cattle Decapitation band spotlight** covers where that band went after he left.
He also drummed in Parasitic from 2004 to 2006, and he has handled vocals and drums in Being Killed since 2007, per Metal Archives.
Pathology was “formed in the beginning of 2006 by Dave Astor,” according to the band’s 2009 **Victory Records signing announcement**. Metal Archives credits the debut, _Surgically Hacked_, to Tim Tiszczenko on bass and vocals, Nick Gervais on guitar and Astor on drums and vocals, with Jeff Forrest producing, and it lists Ramon Mercado as the band’s vocalist in 2006 and 2007. The San Diego Reader has also named Disgorge vocalist Levi Fuselier as a co-founder. Metal Archives lists Fuselier only as the vocalist in 2008, and the band’s bio credits Astor alone, so we’re calling Astor the founder.

## Dave Astor, The Locust and Cattle Decapitation
The early records came out overseas. _Surgically Hacked_ was released in September 2006 on Japan’s Amputated Vein Records. The band’s site now lists it as “Surgically Hacked AKA The Demo,” but it is counted as the first of the 12 albums. In July 2007, Pathology signed with Australia’s Grindhead Records, which released _Incisions of Perverse Debauchery_ in 2008. Comatose Music signed the band in December 2008 and put out _Age of Onset_ in 2009. That record was made at Double Time Studio in El Cajon, with cover art by Pär Olofsson, who has painted many Pathology covers since.

## The Victory Records Years and the 2010 Van Crash
Victory Records signed Pathology on Dec. 12, 2009, when Blabbermouth described the band as a San Diego “death metal/grindcore band.” Three Victory albums followed. _Legacy of the Ancients_ (July 6, 2010) was engineered by Jeff Forrest at Doubletime Studios in San Diego and mixed and mastered by Erik Rutan. _Awaken to the Suffering_ (Sept. 13, 2011) and _The Time of Great Purification_ (Sept. 25, 2012) were both recorded at Lambesis Studios with producer Daniel Castleman.
2010 was the band’s busiest year and its worst. Pathology toured with Nile, with Immolation and Vader, and with Destroyer 666. Late in the year, guitarist Tim Tiszczenko left unexpectedly, and the band had to cancel the last two weeks of the Immolation and Vader run, the San Diego Reader reported.
Then, on Nov. 10, 2010, during the Nile tour, the band’s van hit black ice near Bismarck, North Dakota, on a 1,700-mile drive from St. Paul, Minnesota, to Seattle. **Lambgoat** reported that the van rolled several times. Three members went to the hospital with what were described as minor injuries, but the van, trailer and gear were destroyed, and the rest of the tour was off. “Worst car wreck in my life! Lucky to be alive. Everything is destroyed!” Astor said at the time.

## The Victory Records Years and the 2010 Van Crash
By February 2011, the band had a new van, new gear and a new frontman. Jonathan Huber (ex-I Declare War) replaced “original voice Matti Way, who was unable to tour with the band,” **Blabbermouth reported**. Tiszczenko came back to play alongside his replacement, Kevin Schwartz, and the rebuilt lineup went out opening for Deicide and Belphegor. Astor said in the announcement that he’d seen and met Deicide in San Diego on Halloween 1992. Starting March 24, 2011, Pathology spent five weeks in Europe opening for Obituary and Grave, with stops at Extreme Fest in Paris, Royal Metal Fest in Denmark and Neurotic Deathfest in Holland, and later that year toured North America with Grave and Blood Red Throne.
The lineup kept moving. By December 2012, the San Diego Reader headlined its rundown “After over a dozen lineup changes.” That month, with the three-album Victory deal done, Matti Way and Tim Tiszczenko returned, and Huber and bassist Oscar Ramirez were out. The band called it “the prime Pathology lineup from the Age Of Onset, Legacy era.”

## The Victory Records Years and the 2010 Van Crash
### The album that split the critics
_The Time of Great Purification_ is the record the band keeps coming back to. Astor called it “definitely our heaviest and most technical album to date” when it came out. **Metal Forces** gave it 7.5 out of 10 and said it was “‘Torment In Salvation’ that first really grips you.” **Exclaim!** was harsher, calling it “predictable, with uninspired song structures and repetitive riffs,” while calling 2010’s _Legacy of the Ancients_ “stellar.” The band now calls _The Time of Great Purification_ “the fan-favorite,” and it points to “Tyrannical Decay,” “Imprisoned By Fear” and “A Bleak Future.”

October 29, 2026
The Pathology band is heading into its 20th year with a new singer and a finished record. The San Diego brutal death metal outfit that drummer Dave Astor founded in early 2006 named Tripp Taylor its new vocalist on Aug. 4, said its 13th studio album is in the final stages of mixing and mastering, and has one show on the books: Sunday, Nov. 29, at the Whisky a Go Go in West Hollywood, opening for Fear Factory and Darkest Hour.
Astor is the only founding member still in **Pathology**. Around him, the band has cycled through singers, guitarists and bassists, released records on labels from Japan to Victory Records to Nuclear Blast, survived a van wreck in North Dakota, spent more than five years as a studio-only project and come back with some of the best reviews of its career. This is SDMETAL’s first feature on the band, so here is the whole story, from Astor’s years in The Locust and Cattle Decapitation to what we know, and don’t know, about album 13.

## Dave Astor, The Locust and Cattle Decapitation
Astor was born in San Diego on July 18, 1978, according to **Metal Archives**, and he was part of the city’s extreme music scene long before Pathology existed. Metal Archives lists him as the drummer in The Locust from 1994 to 2001. In Cattle Decapitation, it has him on vocals and bass in 1996 and on drums from 1996 to 2003. He played drums on _Human Jerky_ (1999) and is credited with drums and songwriting on _Homovore_ (2000) and _To Serve Man_ (2002). Pathology’s own bio goes further and calls him a “co-founder of THE LOCUST and CATTLE DECAPITATION.” Our **Cattle Decapitation band spotlight** covers where that band went after he left.
He also drummed in Parasitic from 2004 to 2006, and he has handled vocals and drums in Being Killed since 2007, per Metal Archives.
Pathology was “formed in the beginning of 2006 by Dave Astor,” according to the band’s 2009 **Victory Records signing announcement**. Metal Archives credits the debut, _Surgically Hacked_, to Tim Tiszczenko on bass and vocals, Nick Gervais on guitar and Astor on drums and vocals, with Jeff Forrest producing, and it lists Ramon Mercado as the band’s vocalist in 2006 and 2007. The San Diego Reader has also named Disgorge vocalist Levi Fuselier as a co-founder. Metal Archives lists Fuselier only as the vocalist in 2008, and the band’s bio credits Astor alone, so we’re calling Astor the founder.
texts.3:
## Dave Astor, The Locust and Cattle Decapitation
The early records came out overseas. _Surgically Hacked_ was released in September 2006 on Japan’s Amputated Vein Records. The band’s site now lists it as “Surgically Hacked AKA The Demo,” but it is counted as the first of the 12 albums. In July 2007, Pathology signed with Australia’s Grindhead Records, which released _Incisions of Perverse Debauchery_ in 2008. Comatose Music signed the band in December 2008 and put out _Age of Onset_ in 2009. That record was made at Double Time Studio in El Cajon, with cover art by Pär Olofsson, who has painted many Pathology covers since.
texts.4:
## The Victory Records Years and the 2010 Van Crash
Victory Records signed Pathology on Dec. 12, 2009, when Blabbermouth described the band as a San Diego “death metal/grindcore band.” Three Victory albums followed. _Legacy of the Ancients_ (July 6, 2010) was engineered by Jeff Forrest at Doubletime Studios in San Diego and mixed and mastered by Erik Rutan. _Awaken to the Suffering_ (Sept. 13, 2011) and _The Time of Great Purification_ (Sept. 25, 2012) were both recorded at Lambesis Studios with producer Daniel Castleman.
2010 was the band’s busiest year and its worst. Pathology toured with Nile, with Immolation and Vader, and with Destroyer 666. Late in the year, guitarist Tim Tiszczenko left unexpectedly, and the band had to cancel the last two weeks of the Immolation and Vader run, the San Diego Reader reported.
Then, on Nov. 10, 2010, during the Nile tour, the band’s van hit black ice near Bismarck, North Dakota, on a 1,700-mile drive from St. Paul, Minnesota, to Seattle. **Lambgoat** reported that the van rolled several times. Three members went to the hospital with what were described as minor injuries, but the van, trailer and gear were destroyed, and the rest of the tour was off. “Worst car wreck in my life! Lucky to be alive. Everything is destroyed!” Astor said at the time.
texts.5:
## The Victory Records Years and the 2010 Van Crash
By February 2011, the band had a new van, new gear and a new frontman. Jonathan Huber (ex-I Declare War) replaced “original voice Matti Way, who was unable to tour with the band,” **Blabbermouth reported**. Tiszczenko came back to play alongside his replacement, Kevin Schwartz, and the rebuilt lineup went out opening for Deicide and Belphegor. Astor said in the announcement that he’d seen and met Deicide in San Diego on Halloween 1992. Starting March 24, 2011, Pathology spent five weeks in Europe opening for Obituary and Grave, with stops at Extreme Fest in Paris, Royal Metal Fest in Denmark and Neurotic Deathfest in Holland, and later that year toured North America with Grave and Blood Red Throne.
The lineup kept moving. By December 2012, the San Diego Reader headlined its rundown “After over a dozen lineup changes.” That month, with the three-album Victory deal done, Matti Way and Tim Tiszczenko returned, and Huber and bassist Oscar Ramirez were out. The band called it “the prime Pathology lineup from the Age Of Onset, Legacy era.”
texts.6:
## The Victory Records Years and the 2010 Van Crash
### The album that split the critics
_The Time of Great Purification_ is the record the band keeps coming back to. Astor called it “definitely our heaviest and most technical album to date” when it came out. **Metal Forces** gave it 7.5 out of 10 and said it was “‘Torment In Salvation’ that first really grips you.” **Exclaim!** was harsher, calling it “predictable, with uninspired song structures and repetitive riffs,” while calling 2010’s _Legacy of the Ancients_ “stellar.” The band now calls _The Time of Great Purification_ “the fan-favorite,” and it points to “Tyrannical Decay,” “Imprisoned By Fear” and “A Bleak Future.”

### Pathology Biography by Dave Donnelly
[![Image 1: Incisions of Perverse Debauchery](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/this.src='https://fastly-gce.allmusic.com/images/no_image/album_100x100.png')](https://www.allmusic.com/album/incisions-of-perverse-debauchery-mw0001983371 "Incisions of Perverse Debauchery") Pathology is a brutal American death metal band whose lineup has evolved considerably since their founding in 2006. The group's extreme sound combines gruesome shock imagery with hardcore influences, blastbeats, and distinctive gurgled vocals displayed prominently on the acclaimed 2009 offering Incisions of Perverse Debauchery. After signing to Victory Records that year, they issued the concept album Legacy of the Ancients in 2010. By the time the band had released Lords of Rephaim in 2013, they had woven a trace of traditional death metal into their sound, making their sonic presence even heavier. That direction was pushed to even greater extremes on 2017's self-titled offering, 2019's Reborn to Kill, and 2021's Nuclear Blast-issued Everlasting Plague. Three years later, Unholy Descent arrived on Agonia Records.
Pathology formed in 2006 in San Diego, California at the behest of Dave Astor, founding member and drummer of grindcore act the Locust and death metal group Cattle Decapitation. Astor was joined by vocalists Levi Fuselier and Matti Way, both formerly of legendary California death metal act Disgorge, and guitarist Tim Tiszczenko in the original four-piece lineup.

### Pathology Biography by Dave Donnelly
[![Image 2: Age of Onset](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/this.src='https://fastly-gce.allmusic.com/images/no_image/album_100x100.png')](https://www.allmusic.com/album/age-of-onset-mw0001736415 "Age of Onset") Pathology quickly built up a following in their native San Diego and released their first recording -- a demo CD entitled Surgically Hacked -- within a few months of their formation. The group's first full-length album, Incisions of Perverse Debauchery, was released in February of 2008 on Grindhead Records. Following the release of the album, Mason Gregory joined the band as a second guitarist and vocalist, replacing Fuselier. A second full album, Age of Onset, was released in June of the following year on Comatose Records.
Age of Onset brought Pathology to the attention of large Chicago hardcore/metal label Victory Record, though not before the group parted company with vocalist Matti Way, who was briefly replaced by Pascual Romero. Romero's tenure with the band was short, and he was soon asked to leave in order to accommodate Way's return and the addition of bassist Oscar Ramirez. The group's third album, Legacy of the Ancients, was released on Victory Records in July of 2010. The band was involved in a serious van accident while on tour with Nile in late 2010, forcing them to pull out of the remainder of the tour.

Tim Tiszczenko also left the band briefly, and was replaced by Kevin Schwartz and Stephen Parker, but soon returned in Parker's stead to form a dual guitar partnership with Schwartz. In September of 2011, the band released their fourth full-length record, Awaken to the Suffering, on Victory Records.
[![Image 4: The Time of Great Purification](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/this.src='https://fastly-gce.allmusic.com/images/no_image/album_100x100.png')](https://www.allmusic.com/album/the-time-of-great-purification-mw0002410811 "The Time of Great Purification")Huber left after 2012's The Time of Great Purification. Way returned for the tour and remained in the lineup for the next four years, singing on Lords of Rephaim (2013), Throne of Reign (2014), and Pathology (2017), by which time Tiszczenko also departed and was replaced by guitarist Dan Richardson. The lineup of Astor, Richardson, singer Obie Flett, and bassist Ricky Jackson issued Reborn to Kill in 2019. In 2021, Pathology inked a deal with Nuclear Blast and announced their 11th studio album, the COVID-19 pandemic-inspired concept effort Everlasting Plague, which was released later that November. The uncompromising Unholy Descent, released via Agonia Records, appeared three years later and saw guitarist Daniel Richardson depart for personal reasons, with longtime fan favorite Kevin Schwartz rejoining the band. In 2026, Tripp Taylor took over vocal duties from Obie Flett.

"**Still Swingin'**" is a song by the American rock band Papa Roach released on June 24, 2012 as the first single from their album _The Connection_. The single was well received by fans for the return of the rap-style vocals of the band's early work. The track was produced by Tylias, an indie dubstep and hip-hop producer from the underground music scene. The embrace of this aggregate had polarized opinions, some calling it new and fresh to the songs and another calling it an aberration of their style and even the band, but mostly it was well received. A music video was released on August 30 as lead singer Jacoby Shaddix recovered from a vocal surgery.

## Background information
[edit]
In an interview with _Loudwire_, they asked Jacoby about their upcoming single "Still Swingin'": "You’ve never been ones to shy away from the struggles of trying to make it in music and life. How important of a statement is that song at this point in your career? - It is the most important statement for the band. I think it just says a lot about P-Roach. It’s about my personal life, my highs and lows and what I’ve gone through and I’m a f—in’ survivor dude. I’m a fighter. I think it’s taking a challenge and I’m always willing to step up to it and I’m not going to go out without a fight. And P-Roach, we’re the band that no matter what we’re f—ing up against, we’re gonna prevail. I think we learned that from our early days as a rock and roll band, when every record company told us, ‘No, no, no, no,’ we’re like, ‘F— you, we’re gonna keep on doing it.’ It got us to where we’re at now and we’ve maintained that hustler spirit, that fighter spirit, that warrior spirit. And I think it’s just a great statement to put out as the first single on this record. It’s got the right energy and the right message." The song is currently being used to promote Detroit Tigers broadcasts on Fox Sports Detroit.
The video shows the band performing atop a rooftop along with scenes of a zombie narrative that was suggested by Shaddix's 7-year-old son._[citation needed_]

"**Still Swingin'**" is a song by the American rock band Papa Roach released on June 24, 2012 as the first single from their album _The Connection_. The single was well received by fans for the return of the rap-style vocals of the band's early work. The track was produced by Tylias, an indie dubstep and hip-hop producer from the underground music scene. The embrace of this aggregate had polarized opinions, some calling it new and fresh to the songs and another calling it an aberration of their style and even the band, but mostly it was well received. A music video was released on August 30 as lead singer Jacoby Shaddix recovered from a vocal surgery.

Papa Roach is a hard rock band from Vacaville, California, United States. Formed in 1993, it consists of Jacoby Shaddix (vocals), Jerry Horton (guitar), Tobin Esperance (bass), and Tony Palermo (drums).
Tony, previously of Unwritten Law, joined the band permanently in 2008; the move came after the departure of one of the band's founding members, Dave Buckner. The band has sold more than 10 million album copies worldwide and are known for their hits "Last Resort", "Scars", "Forever", and "Lifeline", among others.
The group had mostly regional success until their breakthrough with the hit single "Last Resort". That song came from their first major label album, 'Infest', and has remained a fan favorite for years.
The band's latest album titled Metamorphosis was released March 24th, 2009, with the singles "Lifeline" and "Hollywood Whore" available at digital retailers. They released a live album w/ 5 new tracks August 31, 2010 named "Time for Annihilation…On the Record and On the Road", with the first singles being "Kick In The Teeth" and "No Matter What".
The Still Swinging Songfacts reports that Papa Roach's eighth studio album, The Connection, was recorded at the band's hometown studio, The Red House in Sacramento, California. The long player was produced by James Michael (Sixx:A.
M., Halestorm) and John Feldmann (Panic at the Disco, The Used, Escape the Fate). The album was released on October 2, 2012. The first single off the album was "Still Swingin'" which was a top 5 hit on the Modern Rock Tracks chart peaking at #3.

## Breakthrough Moment
Papa Roach achieved significant mainstream recognition with their major-label debut _Infest_, released in 2000 on Geffen Records. The album marked a decisive shift in profile, establishing the band as legitimate players in the nu metal and rap rock crossover that had begun to dominate rock radio. _Infest_ became the vehicle for their expanded reach, moving them from a group with regional credibility to one with national and international visibility. The album’s success established Papa Roach as a permanent fixture in the rock and metal landscape of the 2000s.

## Peak Era
The period from 2000 through the mid-2000s represented Papa Roach’s most commercially dominant and creatively ambitious phase. Following _Infest_, the band released _Lovehatetragedy_ in 2002 and _Getting Away With Murder_ in 2004, each demonstrating the band’s ability to refine their approach while maintaining their core sonic identity. The consistency of output during these years—three full-length albums across four years—kept Papa Roach in the touring and album-sales conversation during an era when rock and metal remained substantial commercial forces. The band’s willingness to tour extensively and engage with the growing nu metal festival circuit cemented their position as more than a one-album success story.

## Musical Style
Papa Roach’s sound is built on the intersection of rap-inflected vocal delivery and rock instrumentation rooted in heavy, distorted guitars and prominent drums. Jacoby Shaddix’s vocal approach alternates between rapped verses and melodic, often sung choruses, a technique that became central to the late-1990s rap rock aesthetic. Jerry Horton’s guitar work combines downtuned riffs with occasional melodic passages, while Tobin Esperance’s bass provides rhythmic anchor and low-end weight. Dave Buckner’s drumming emphasizes groove and pocket, supporting the band’s hybrid approach rather than pursuing purely technical virtuosity. The band’s instrumentation and production choices reflect the late-1990s and early-2000s nu metal template: heavily processed drums, layered guitars, and a mix that foregrounds both rap and rock elements without fully prioritizing one over the other.

## Major Albums
### Infest (2000)
Papa Roach’s major-label breakthrough album, _Infest_ introduced the band to a mass audience and established their signature blend of rap and metal as commercially viable. The album became the band’s highest-profile statement during the peak of the nu metal commercial cycle.

## Major Albums
### Lovehatetragedy (2002)
Released two years after _Infest_, this album demonstrated Papa Roach’s ability to sustain momentum, deepening their musical palette while remaining faithful to their core sound and appeal.

## Major Albums
### Getting Away With Murder (2004)
The third full-length studio album continued Papa Roach’s commercial and creative presence, arriving during the still-thriving rap rock moment of the mid-2000s.

## Major Albums
### The Paramour Sessions (2006)
This album marked a notable shift in approach, suggesting the band’s willingness to explore different production and songwriting contexts as their core fanbase matured.

## Major Albums
### Metamorphosis (2009)
Released in the post-nu metal commercial peak era, _Metamorphosis_ represented Papa Roach’s attempt to remain relevant as broader rock trends shifted away from the late-1990s aesthetic that had birthed them.

## Major Albums
### F.E.A.R. (2015)
Album released in the streaming era, demonstrating Papa Roach’s continued commitment to studio recording nearly two decades into their career.

## Signature Songs
*   Lead track and defining song from _Infest_, establishing the band’s mainstream identity and remaining their most widely recognized recording.  
*   Songs from their early major-label period established the band’s rap-rock formula and received significant rock radio and MTV exposure.  
*   The band’s consistent touring presence ensured multiple tracks from their catalog became familiar to rock and metal audiences throughout the 2000s.  
*   Later-era releases demonstrate the band’s evolution and their attempt to maintain relevance across changing musical tastes.

## Influence on Rock
Papa Roach emerged during and contributed to the commercialization of rap rock and nu metal in the late 1990s and early 2000s. Their sustained presence in the music industry across multiple decades indicates the durability of the hybrid rap-rock model, even as broader commercial and critical trends shifted away from nu metal’s peak moment. The band’s consistent touring schedule and album releases across the 2010s and 2020s suggest that rap rock, despite its decline in mainstream radio, retained enough cultural footprint and fanbase loyalty to sustain bands that had established early popularity within the genre. Papa Roach’s career demonstrates the viability of the alternative-to-metal pipeline for bands willing to embrace both vocal approaches and instrumental styles.

## Legacy
Papa Roach’s legacy is primarily as reliable representatives of late-1990s and early-2000s rap rock and nu metal rather than as innovators who fundamentally altered rock music. Their greatest impact lies in their demonstration that the rap-rock crossover could sustain a major international touring career and album-sales presence across multiple decades. The band’s consistent presence since their 1993 formation—active through 2022 and beyond—places them in the category of bands that built careers by maintaining fidelity to their core audience rather than chasing critical reinvention. In the streaming era, their catalog remains accessible and familiar to generations of rock and metal listeners who came of age during the nu metal 2000s.

## Fun Facts
*   The band’s name, Papa Roach, originated from a family friend and remained unchanged despite early shifts in personnel and musical approach.  
*   Vacaville, California, the band’s origin city, remains relatively uncommon as a birthplace for internationally significant rock acts, making Papa Roach’s emergence from the region notable for local music history.  
*   The band’s early album _Old Friends From Young Years_ (1997) predated their major-label signing and represented their independent foundation before _Infest_ brought mainstream recognition.  
*   Papa Roach’s longevity across three decades reflects both their fanbase loyalty and their pragmatic approach to album releases and touring, remaining active even as broader rock commercial forces declined.

# Papa Roach
### About
*   alternative

Papa Roach is a hard rock band from Vacaville, California, United States. Formed in 1993, it consists of Jacoby Shaddix (vocals), Jerry Horton (guitar), Tobin Esperance (bass), and Tony Palermo (drums).
Tony, previously of Unwritten Law, joined the band permanently in 2008; the move came after the departure of one of the band's founding members, Dave Buckner. The band has sold more than 10 million album copies worldwide and are known for their hits "Last Resort", "Scars", "Forever", and "Lifeline", among others.
The group had mostly regional success until their breakthrough with the hit single "Last Resort". That song came from their first major label album, 'Infest', and has remained a fan favorite for years.
The band's latest album titled Metamorphosis was released March 24th, 2009, with the singles "Lifeline" and "Hollywood Whore" available at digital retailers. They released a live album w/ 5 new tracks August 31, 2010 named "Time for Annihilation…On the Record and On the Road", with the first singles being "Kick In The Teeth" and "No Matter What".
The Still Swinging Songfacts reports that Papa Roach's eighth studio album, The Connection, was recorded at the band's hometown studio, The Red House in Sacramento, California. The long player was produced by James Michael (Sixx:A.
M., Halestorm) and John Feldmann (Panic at the Disco, The Used, Escape the Fate). The album was released on October 2, 2012. The first single off the album was "Still Swingin'" which was a top 5 hit on the Modern Rock Tracks chart peaking at #3.

2010edit
The city had a population of 1,307,402 according to the 2010 census, distributed over a land area of 372.1 square miles (963.7 km2).[130] The urban area of San Diego had a total population of 2,956,746, making it the third-largest in the state, after those of Los Angeles and San Francisco.

The 2010 population represented an increase of just under 7% from the 1,223,400 people reported in 2000.[126] The population density was 3,771.9 inhabitants per square mile (1,456.3/km2). The racial makeup of San Diego was 58.9% White, 6.7% Black, 0.6% Native American, 15.9% Asian (5.9% Filipino, 2.7% Chinese, 2.5% Vietnamese, 1.3% Indian, 1.0% Korean, 0.7% Japanese, 0.4% Laotian, 0.3% Cambodian, 0.1% Thai). 0.5% Pacific Islander (0.2% Guamanian, 0.1% Samoan, 0.1% Native Hawaiian), 12.3% from other races, and 5.1% from two or more races. 28.8% of the population was Hispanic or Latino (of any race);[126][131] 24.9% of the total population was of Mexican heritage, 1.4% Spanish and 0.6% Puerto Rican. The median age of Hispanic residents was 27.5 years, compared to 35.1 years overall and 41.6 years among non-Hispanic whites; Hispanic San Diegans were the largest group under the age of 18, while non-Hispanic whites constituted 63.1% of population 55 and older.
Map of racial distribution in San Diego, 2010 U.S. Census. Each dot is 25 people: ⬤ Non-Hispanic White ⬤ Black ⬤ Asian ⬤ Hispanic ⬤ Other

As of January 2019, the San Diego City and County had the fifth-largest homeless population among major cities in the United States, with 8,102 people experiencing homelessness.[132] In the city of San Diego, 4,887 individuals were experiencing homelessness according to the 2020 count.[133] A December 11, 2023, article in The San Diego Union-Tribune by Blake Nelson reports a notable decline in the homeless population in downtown San Diego, specifically in the urban core. According to data from the Downtown San Diego Partnership, the number of individuals living outside or in vehicles has reached a two-year low, standing at approximately 1,200 as of last month. The decrease is attributed to the implementation of the city's camping ban and the concerted efforts to establish new shelters. While enforcement has led to relatively few individuals being punished, the threat of legal consequences appears to have played a role in the reduction.[134]
Barrio Logan is a Chicano cultural hub and ethnic enclave.
In 2000 there were 451,126 households, out of which 30.2% had children under the age of 18 living with them, 44.6% were married couples living together, 11.4% had a female householder with no husband present, and 39.8% were non-families. Households made up of individuals account for 28.0%, and 7.4% had someone living alone who was 65 years of age or older. The average household size was 2.61, and the average family size was 3.30.
